memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But Moses said, "Pardon your servant, Lord. Please send someone else." Then the Lord's anger burned against Moses and he said, "What about your brother, Aaron the Levite? I know he can speak well. He is already on his way to meet you, and he will be glad to see you."" - Exodus 4:13-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At last the real objection comes out. Moses is no longer asking questions about ability. He simply says: please send someone else.

And for the first time, God's anger burns. Why here and not earlier? Because the earlier objections were fear seeking reassurance, and God answered each one patiently. This one is refusal after every objection has been answered. There is a point where honest wrestling becomes plain unwillingness.

Yet look at what God's anger produces. Not rejection, not punishment — Aaron. God gives him help. Even His displeasure serves His purpose.

Notice too the timing. Aaron was already on his way. Before Moses ever asked, God had set the answer in motion. That is how far ahead of us God works.

Do not let this go by too quickly, though. Aaron would later make the golden calf. God's concession to Moses' reluctance carried a real cost. Sometimes God gives us what we insist on, and we live with the consequences.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have my honest questions quietly become excuses?
2. Where has God already provided help I have not yet recognised?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, forgive me when my questions are really refusals. Give me a willing heart and thank You for the help You have already prepared. Amen.
